text:
A: Hiya! Oh, hello again, sort of. I saw your photo earlier, all those books behind you!
B: Hello. Yes, that's most of them. There's more in the back bedroom.
A: I'm Joanne, Taunton. I've just been talking to a lovely lad from Bridgwater, mechanic. Sorry, you don't need to know that!
B: That's alright. I'm Helen, I'm in Otley. West Yorkshire.
A: Oh, I've never been up that way. Is it pretty?
B: It is, yes. There's a hill called the Chevin right above the town. I walk up it most Sundays, early, before anyone else is about.
A: Oh, that sounds proper lovely. I walk my dog up the Quantocks when my back lets me. So what do you do, with all them books?
B: Erm, I'm an archivist. University library in Leeds. Old letters and diaries mostly, cataloguing them.
A: Ooh, that's fascinating. Do you ever find anything juicy? Sorry, that's probably a terrible question.
B: No, it's the question everyone asks. And sometimes, yes. You get a very polite letter from a mill owner's wife and then a second one to her sister saying what she actually thinks of him.
A: Ha! Oh, I love that. Nothing changes, does it?
B: Not really, no.
A: I was a vet nurse, for twenty-odd years. Not now, my back went. I help at a cat rescue a few hours a week, which, you know, keeps me sane.
B: That must be hard work. Emotionally, I mean.
A: Erm, it was, yeah. People always asked for me when their pet was being put to sleep. Which is a funny thing to be good at, isn't it? But I'd rather it was someone who cared. Sorry, that's a bit heavy for a Tuesday!
B: No, I think that's quite a thing to be good at, actually.
A: Oh, that's kind. Have you got family?
B: A daughter, Isla. She's nine.
A: Oh, lovely age. Mine are twenty-two and nineteen, my Ellie's in Cardiff at uni. She only rings when she wants money, mind!
B: I've got that to look forward to, then.
A: Oh, you have! Do you do anything for yourself? You look like a reader.
B: Reading, yes. And I draw plants, pencil and watercolour. And I go to evensong sometimes, at Ripon or Leeds Minster. I like choral music.
A: Oh, I sing in a choir! Nothing posh, mind. We're doing an ABBA medley for the summer concert.
B: That's not exactly evensong.
A: No! Although "Thank You for the Music" is sort of a hymn, if you squint.
B: I'll give you that one.
A: Do you sing?
B: Only in church, at the back, quietly.
A: That still counts! Oh, I think we're nearly out of time.
B: It's gone quick.
